8 + [16 – {7 + 4 – (9 of 3 + 6 – 4 × 7)}]

questions.question: \(\frac{3}{4}\; + \;\frac{5}{2}\left[ {\frac{1}{4}\; \times \;\left( {\frac{8}{5} - \frac{4}{3}} \right)} \right]\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below :
Step-1 : Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,
Step-2 : Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,
Step-3 : Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,
Step-4 : Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.

\( \Rightarrow \frac{3}{4}{\rm{}} + {\rm{}}\frac{5}{2}\left[ {\frac{1}{4}{\rm{}} \times {\rm{\;}}\left( {\frac{8}{5} - \frac{4}{3}} \right)} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{3}{4}{\rm{}} + {\rm{}}\frac{5}{2}\left[ {\frac{1}{4}{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}\left( {\frac{{24{\rm{\;}} - {\rm{\;}}20}}{{15}}} \right)} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \;\frac{3}{{4{\rm{\;}}}}{\rm{}} + {\rm{}}\frac{5}{2}{\rm{\;}}\left[ {\frac{1}{4}{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}\frac{4}{{15}}} \right]\)

⇒ 3/4 + [5/2 × 1/15]

⇒ 3/4 + 1/6

⇒ (9 + 2)/12

⇒ 11/12

questions.question: \(\frac{{675 \times 675 \times 675 + 325 \times 325 \times 325}}{{675 \times 675 + 325 \times 325 - 675 \times 325}}=?\)
questions.solution:
We have,

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 - ab + b2)

Suppose a = 675 and b = 325

⇒ (a3 + b3) / [(a2 + b2 - ab)]

= [(a + b)(a2 - ab + b2)] / [(a2 + b2 - ab)] = (a + b)  = (675 + 325) = 1000

Concept Used:

BODMAS = Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction

Calculation:

⇒ 9 ×  4 of 3 ÷ 2 - 5 × Q + 2 × 3 = 10

⇒ 9 ×  12 ÷ 2 - 5 × Q + 2 × 3 = 10

⇒ 9 × 6 - 5 × Q + 2 × 3 = 10

⇒ 54 - 5Q + 6 = 10

questions.question: \(\frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {3\frac{1}{5} - \left\{ {\frac{5}{6} - \left( {3\frac{4}{5} \div 9\frac{1}{2}} \right)} \right\}} \right]\) is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below∶
Step-1: Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

Step-2: Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3: Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4: Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.

\(\frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {3\frac{1}{5} - \left\{ {\frac{5}{6} - \left( {3\frac{4}{5} \div 9\frac{1}{2}} \right)} \right\}} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {\frac{{16}}{5} - \left\{ {\frac{5}{6} - \left( {\frac{{19}}{5} \div \frac{{19}}{2}} \right)} \right\}} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {\frac{{16}}{5} - \left\{ {\frac{5}{6} - \left( {\frac{{19}}{5} \times \frac{2}{{19}}} \right)} \right\}} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {\frac{{16}}{5} - \left\{ {\frac{5}{6} - \frac{2}{5}} \right\}} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {\frac{{16}}{5} - \frac{{25 - 12}}{{30}}} \right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{17}}{{30}} + \left[ {\frac{{16}}{5} - \frac{{13}}{{30}}} \right]\)

⇒ [17/30] + [(96 - 13)/30]

⇒ [17/30] + [83/30]

⇒ 10/3

questions.question: By Interchanging the given two numbers (Not digits) which of the following equation will be correct? 5 and 9 I. 7 × 9 + 5 – 8 ÷ 4 = 42 II. 9 × 3 + 5 ÷ 1 – 4 = 20
questions.questionHtml:
By Interchanging the given two numbers (Not digits) which of the following equation will be correct?

5 and 9

I. 7 × 9 + 5 – 8 ÷ 4 = 42

II. 9 × 3 + 5 ÷ 1 – 4 = 20
questions.solution:
I. 7 × 9 + 5 – 8 ÷ 4 = 42

After interchanging 5 and 9, we get:

7 × 5 + 9 – 8 ÷ 4 = 42

⇒ 35 + 9 - 2 = 42

⇒ 44 - 2 = 42

⇒ 42 = 42

II. 9 × 3 + 5 ÷ 1 – 4 = 20

After interchanging 5 and 9, we get:

5 × 3 + 9 ÷ 1 – 4 = 20

⇒ 15 + 9 - 4 = 20

⇒ 24 - 4 = 20

⇒ 20 = 20

Hence, ‘Both I and II’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: If \(\frac{1}{4}\) of \(\frac{4}{5} + \frac{9}{2}\) of \(\frac{17}{3} - \frac{3}{10}\) = p, then what is the value of p?

questions.solution:
Given:

 \(\frac{1}{4}\) of \(\frac{4}{5} + \frac{9}{2}\) of \(\frac{17}{3} - \frac{3}{10}\) = p

Concept used:

Calculation:

\({1\over4} \space of \space {4\over5}+{9\over2} \space of \space {17\over3}-{3\over10}=p\)

\({1\over4} \times {4\over5}+{9\over2} \times {17\over3}-{3\over10}=p\)

\({1\over5} +{51\over2}-{3\over10}=p\)

\({(2+255-3)\over10}=p\)

\(p = {254\over10} = {127\over5}\)

∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: If sign ‘+’ is interchanged with ‘÷’ and number ‘2’ is interchanged with ‘6’, which of the following would be correct?

By interchanging ‘+’ and ‘÷’ and ‘2’ and ‘6’

Option 1:

4 + 6 is not equal to 8

Option 2:

6 ÷ 8 + 2 = 6

3/4 + 2 is not equal to 6

Option 3:

6 ÷ 8 + 2 = 8

3/4 + 2 is not equal to 8

Option 4:

6 ÷ 2 + 8 = 11

3 + 8 = 11

11 = 11

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.
